10.1002_smll.76427: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are significantly hindered by internal short circuits resulting from uncontrolled lithium dendrite growth. To address this challenge, we have developed an innovative polymer to modify conventional commercial separators, thereby mitigating lithium dendrite proliferation. This polymer is synthesized through the copolymerization of three monomers: poly(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate (PEGMA), tetramethyltetravinylcyclotetrasiloxane (TTCS), and 2‐ureido‐4[1H]‐pyrimidinone methyl methacrylate (UpyMA). The dynamic hydrogen bonds present in the UpyMA monomer confer self‐healing properties to the polymer, while the PEO chains in PEGMA facilitate enhanced Li + transport. Concurrently, TTCS interacts with Li + to improve lithium‐ion transfer, collectively contributing to the effective suppression of lithium dendrite growth. Moreover, the functional groups within the polymer not only modulate the solvation structure of the electrolyte but also partially react with Li to aid in the formation of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). This results in the creation of an organic/inorganic‐rich hybrid SEI that bolsters the stability of LMBs. Following the modification of the separator, the Li||Li symmetric cell demonstrates stable cycling for over 700 h. The Li||NCM811 full cell achieves stable cycling for 300 cycles with a capacity retention rate of 83.6%.
10.1016_j.jcou.2026.103576: Synthesis of olefins, such as ethylene, via electrochemical CO2RR offers a sustainable route using renewable electricity. Copper is a suitable catalyst, yet selectivity to C2+ products is limited by Bronsted-acidic intermediates that hinder C-C coupling. Highly concentrated electrolytes (e.g., 10M KOH) can suppress local acidity but accelerate carbonate formation and hinder the performance. Herein, we introduce a BaO integrated CuO catalyst with built-in local basicity at the BaO/CuO interfaces, directly fabricated onto a gas-diffusion electrode. During CO₂RR process, BaO provides O²⁻ sites that generate local -OH and tune the Cu electronic structure, promoting C2+ formation. In a 3 cm² zerogap membrane–electrode assembly operated with 1 M KOH, the BaO/CuO3PBAir cathode achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 42% for ethylene and 72% for total C2+ products at 166 mA cm⁻². These results highlight that integrating basic-oxide promoters at Cu-based interfaces in a binder-free cathode enables efficient CO₂ electroreduction in zero-gap cells.
10.1021_acsenergylett.5c03341: Sn–Pb perovskites are essential for achieving efficient single-junction solar cells and all-perovskite tandem solar cells (APTSCs). Although Sn oxidation and defective surfaces were once major limitations, recent advances in intrinsic material quality have largely mitigated these issues. As a result, the HTL-related interface is now regarded as the primary bottleneck for device performance. To address the intrinsic drawbacks of PEDOT:PSS, chemical surface modification and additive strategies have been widely applied, and alternative HTLs, like polymeric, inorganic, or small-molecule HTLs, have also gained attention. These approaches offer improved energy-level alignment, high transparency, and enhanced chemical durability, leading to higher short-circuit current density and longer operational lifetime in both single-junction and tandem devices. In this Perspective, we highlight the key criteria and practical effects of HTL materials suitable for Sn–Pb perovskites.
10.1038_s41467-026-75482-y: Enhancing high-capacity silicon-graphite negative electrodes and high-voltage positive electrodes is crucial for improving specific energy of lithium-ion batteries. However, challenges like large volume change in silicon-graphite electrode and electrolyte decomposition at high voltage compromise electrochemical stability. Furthermore, sluggish Li+ exchange between electrolytes and electrodes severely hinders electrochemical kinetics. Herein, we design an anion-rich electrolyte with high oxidation resistance and rapid desolvation behavior, which enabling the formation of effective interphases for improving electrochemical performance. The optimized electrolyte allows silicon-graphite electrode to achieve 1838.9 mAh g−1 capacity at 0.1 C with a long-term electrochemical stability, while a lithium-rich layered oxide positive electrode maintains 72.3% retention after 600 cycles at 1 C. The designed electrolyte with nonflammability also enhances safety in pouch cells after nail penetration. This design significantly improves cycling stability in high-specific-energy batteries, reaching specific energy of 278 Wh kg−1 for graphite | |lithium-rich layered oxide and 355 Wh kg−1 for silicon-graphite | |Ni-rich layer oxide pouch cells, calculated based on all cell components (positive electrode, negative electrode, separator and electrolyte). The design of the high-voltage electrolyte introduces a feasible approach to formulate a suitable solvation structure for high-specific-energy batteries. Enhancing high-capacity silicon-graphite negative electrodes and high-voltage positive electrodes is crucial for improving specific energy of lithium batteries. Here, the authors design an anion-rich electrolyte with high oxidation resistance and rapid desolvation that forms effective interphases and improves electrochemical performance.
10.1039_d6ta04596k: Low-T sintering (650 °C) and 4wt% Yb 3+ doping in α-Al 2 O 3 preserve nanoscale interfaces, boosting proton conduction via –OH pathways. This yields 0.167 S cm −1 conductivity and 696 mW cm −2 power at 550 °C with >50 h stable operation.
